items.followUp: State two roles of mitosis in living organisms.

rubric.why: Mitosis enables an organism to grow and to repair or replace cells.
rubric.description: Gives one valid significance of mitosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct role, such as growth, repair, replacement of damaged or worn-out cells, or asexual reproduction.

rubric.why: A further significance is that mitosis maintains chromosome number in daughter cells or supports asexual reproduction.
rubric.description: Gives a second, distinct significance of mitosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another correct role. Do not award twice for the same role.

modelAnswer: Mitosis increases the number of cells, allowing an organism to grow.
It repairs tissues by replacing damaged or worn-out cells.
It also maintains the chromosome number in daughter cells.

items.followUp: State two differences between mitosis and meiosis.

rubric.why: A bivalent is a pair of homologous chromosomes joined together during meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a paired set of homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: The paired chromosomes contain four chromatids in total, giving the structure the name tetrad.
rubric.description: Explains why a bivalent is called a tetrad.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the name to its four chromatids.

modelAnswer: A bivalent is a pair of homologous chromosomes that come together during meiosis.
It is called a tetrad because it consists of four chromatids—two from each homologous chromosome.

items.followUp: Sketch and label the structure of an ATP molecule.

rubric.why: ATP contains adenine attached to a ribose sugar; together these form adenosine.
rubric.description: Shows the adenine and ribose components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if both adenine and ribose (or sugar) are shown and labelled.

rubric.why: Three phosphate groups are attached to the ribose part of ATP.
rubric.description: Shows three phosphate groups attached to adenosine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing and labelling three phosphate groups linked to the adenine–ribose part.

modelAnswer: Draw and label the parts in this order: adenine — ribose — phosphate — phosphate — phosphate.
Show adenine attached to ribose; label this combined part “adenosine.”
Attach three phosphate groups in a chain to the ribose, and label the molecule “ATP.”

items.followUp: Name the raw materials and products of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Glucose is a product of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for glucose or sugar.

rubric.why: Oxygen is also released during photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: The products of photosynthesis are glucose and oxygen.
Carbon dioxide and water are used to make glucose, and oxygen is released.

items.followUp: What is the role of an enzyme’s active site?

rubric.why: The active site is a particular region or part of an enzyme.
rubric.description: Identifies the active site as a region of an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a specific part or region of the enzyme.

rubric.why: The substrate binds at the active site, where the enzyme-catalysed reaction takes place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the substrate binds or fits there, or that the reaction occurs there.

modelAnswer: The active site is the specific region of an enzyme to which its substrate binds.
The enzyme-catalysed reaction takes place at the active site.

items.followUp: Define enzyme and explain how it acts on a substrate.

rubric.why: A substrate is the substance on which an enzyme acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the substrate as the substance or reactant acted on by an enzyme.

rubric.why: A product is the substance formed by a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the product as the substance formed or produced by a reaction.

modelAnswer: A substrate is the substance on which an enzyme acts.
A product is the substance formed as a result of a chemical reaction.

items.followUp: Write two more characteristics of enzymes.

rubric.why: Enzymes act as biological catalysts and speed up chemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct characteristic, such as being biological catalysts, mostly proteins, or being specific to their substrates.

rubric.why: Enzymes have other characteristic properties, including specificity, being reusable, and sensitivity to temperature and pH.
rubric.description: Gives a second, distinct characteristic of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another correct characteristic. Do not award twice for the same property.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions.
They are specific: each enzyme acts on a particular substrate.
Enzymes are not used up in the reactions they catalyse.

items.followUp: What are unsaturated fatty acids, and give one benefit of including them in a diet?

rubric.why: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon–carbon double bonds; their carbon atoms are joined by single bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they contain no double bonds or only single bonds between carbon atoms.

rubric.why: Excess saturated fat can raise blood cholesterol and increase the risk of heart or cardiovascular disease.
rubric.description: Gives a drawback of saturated fatty acids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct drawback, such as raising blood cholesterol or increasing heart-disease risk.

modelAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have only single bonds between their carbon atoms and no carbon–carbon double bonds.
A drawback of consuming too much saturated fat is that it can raise blood cholesterol and increase the risk of coronary heart disease.
